implementation.name: original-v2-pipeline-1f1b
implementation.scope: Original four-stage eight-microbatch 1F1B schedule; activation presence computed from source F/B operations, with schematic equal slots.
implementation.question: Why does alternating forward and backward reduce saved activations?

purpose: Expose each microbatch activation's lifetime and distinguish reduced memory residency from persistent pipeline bubbles.
storyboard: Begin with empty per-stage activation sets and the original schedule as reference.
Complete each source column; forward saves and backward consumes the matching microbatch activation.
Retain activations through idle columns and show the current set plus running peak.
Drain every activation and compare computed peaks with the original right-hand bars and GPipe reference.
guard: Parse operations from the verified artwork. Validate forward and backward dependencies before each slot, one forward/backward per microbatch per stage, empty final live sets, and peaks matching the source bars. Count microbatch activations, not bytes; timing is schematic, not measured.
